Exercise B

Reading: Skills & Notices

Read the texts below, then answer the questions — just like Reading Parts 1 and 2 in the real MSA exam.

Part 1 — Match the Student to the First-Aid Skill

CPR (chest compressions): If someone's heart has stopped, you press hard on their chest again and again to keep the blood moving until an ambulance arrives.

The recovery position: If someone is unconscious but still breathing, you turn them carefully onto their side so they can breathe safely and do not choke.

Treating burns: If someone burns their hand, you hold it under cool running water for several minutes to take the heat out of the skin.

Stopping bleeding: If someone has a deep cut, you press a clean cloth firmly onto the wound to stop the blood and then wrap a bandage around it.

1 Lena's little brother touched a hot cooker and hurt his hand. She needs to know about .

Exercise C

Writing: Course Application

To join the first-aid course, fill in the short application below. Answer each question in 2–4 full sentences. This section is graded by your teacher, not automatically.

First-Aid Course — Application Form

Please answer all three questions in your own words:

1. Why would you like to take this first-aid course?

2. Have you ever helped someone who was hurt or unwell? What happened, or what would you do?

3. Which first-aid skill would you most like to learn, and why?
